title: Liverpool fan group confirms protests ‘inside and outside Anfield’ over ticket price rise
content:
Liverpool supporters’ union Spirit of Shankly (SOS) has announced protests “inside and outside Anfield” over the club’s planned ticket price increases — starting with next Saturday’s home clash with Fulham.

It is also calling on fans not to spend money inside the ground and to delay renewing season tickets to “send a message” to owner Fenway Sports Group.

The club recently announced inflation-linked price rises for each of the next three seasons. With an increase of three per cent for 2026-27, adult general admission tickets, which currently cost between £39 and £61, are set to go up between £1.25 and £1.75 per game. Adult season tickets, which currently cost between £713 and £904, would increase between £21.50 and £27 — up to £1.42 more per game.

That triggered an angry reaction from Liverpool’s Supporters’ Board, who had called for a two-year prize freeze. SOS hosted an open meeting online last week and carried out a survey to gauge the mood before formulating a co-ordinated response with other fan groups.

SOS spokesman Gareth Roberts said: “This is no longer about consultation. That opportunity has been and gone. This is about action.

“The direction is clear: protests will take place. If the club does not value supporter voices, we will make ourselves difficult to ignore. The Supporters’ Board has formally informed the club that action is coming. Now it is on all of us to back it.

“Protests inside and outside Anfield have been discussed. It is agreed they need to happen. This will not be limited to one game. Action will take place across home and away fixtures, starting with Fulham at Anfield and escalating from there.”

Liverpool, who had frozen prices in eight of the previous 10 seasons, say that matchday operating costs at Anfield have increased by 85 per cent since 2016-17.

However, SOS believe that the money the club generates from both media and commercial income streams means there is no need to crank up ticket prices.

“If the club wants to take more from supporters, then supporters can give less back,” Roberts added.

“We are asking fans, where possible, not to spend money inside the ground. Spend your money with local, independent businesses around Anfield instead. This is a small act, but if enough people do it, it sends a clear message. Supporters have also suggested delaying season ticket renewals until close to the deadline. We support that.

“This decision sits with ownership. They have made the call. They can reverse it. We will be taking steps to make sure that message reaches them directly.

“This is Liverpool FC’s owners locking in price rises for years to come and removing meaningful annual scrutiny from supporters. No other Premier League is doing this. If it goes unchallenged, it sets a precedent. Not just for Liverpool, but across the game.

“At the end of these three years, it would be a fifth increase in six seasons. Tickets heading towards £70. Season tickets beyond £1,000.”
